repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
fired := false
if (fired == true) {
    wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == false)
    fired = false
}
wait until((#Hall_Motion).motionSensor_motion == true)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(100, 0)
delay(3 SEC)
(#Hall_Light).light_moveToBrightness(0, 0)
fired = true

diagnosis.summary: The candidate implements a periodic `if` check instead of a rising-edge wait. At t=100ms, the motion sensor was already true, but the candidate only evaluates its guard at the start of the next wrapper period (t=1000ms), missing the rising edge event that the IR waits for.
diagnosis.change_summary: Changed the script to use a blocking rising-edge wait (`wait until(P)`) followed by the body and a state flag (`fired`), wrapped in a `period` of 1000ms. This ensures the automation blocks until the rising edge occurs, then executes the body exactly once per cycle, matching the IR's `cycle { wait(..., rising); BODY }` structure.
